name: New Delhi
summary: Seven cities stacked on one plain. C More meets every inbound guest at Indira Gandhi International Airport and starts the programme among Lutyens’ avenues, Qutub Minar, Humayun’s Tomb, and the lanes of Shahjahanabad.
highlights: India Gate and the diplomatic enclave
Red Fort, Chandni Chowk, and Jama Masjid

name: Jaipur
summary: The Pink City, planned on a grid and still lived in. Amber Fort, City Palace, Jantar Mantar, and the gem bazaars are the heart of almost every north India programme C More writes.

name: Agra
summary: The Mughal capital on the Yamuna. The Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, and Akbar’s tomb at Sikandra, with Fatehpur Sikri a short drive away.

name: Jodhpur
summary: The Blue City under Mehrangarh. A natural gateway to the desert road for camel safaris and the forts further west.

name: Jaisalmer
summary: A living sandstone fort on the edge of the Thar. Camel safaris, dunes, and havelis are how C More’s Rajasthan desert programmes spend their nights.

name: Ranakpur
summary: A marble Jain temple complex in the Aravalli hills, usually visited on the drive between Jodhpur and Udaipur.

name: Ranthambore
summary: Tiger reserve and ruined fort. C More uses it for short luxury breaks and as a wildlife pause inside longer Rajasthan routes.

name: Udaipur
summary: Lakes, palaces, and the white city in the south of Rajasthan. A frequent last stop on camel-safari and honeymoon routes.

name: Kerala
summary: Backwaters, spice hills, and Ayurveda. Kumarakom, Kochi, Alleppey, and Thekkady are the places C More’s coconut and Ayurveda holidays actually stay.

name: Varanasi
summary: The river city on the Ganges, and the start of the Buddhist and temple circuits that continue to Sarnath, Bodhgaya, and Khajuraho.

name: Ladakh
summary: High desert and monasteries. The Hemis festival programme is built around Leh and the masked dances at Hemis Gompa.

name: Pushkar
summary: A small pilgrimage town that becomes the Pushkar Fair each November: camels, cattle, competitions, and the holy lake.

name: Srinagar
summary: Dal Lake, houseboats, Mughal gardens, and the road to Gulmarg, Sonmarg, and Pahalgam. C More’s Kashmir programme starts here.

name: Mumbai
summary: The harbour city that opens several C More circuits: Elephanta, Aurangabad’s caves, Goa, and the long North & West India with Nepal tour.

name: Kolkata
summary: The eastern start of C More’s Golden Triangle — East India tour, before Bhubaneswar, Puri, and the Northeast.

name: Port Blair
summary: The capital of the Andamans, and the start of C More’s island programme through Havelock and Neil.
